Complete build.ts inspected: fetch schemastore.org/api/json/catalog.json -> response.json + assertions -> generated schemas/package.json; filesystem removal is restricted to local schemas output
No install/activation path binds build.ts to endpoint startup
limits: Build-time catalog content and schema URLs are data dependencies, not authenticated provenance claims.

assessment.trigger: Activation registers document-change listener; user/config can disable or invoke save commands.
assessment.reason: Complete small entrypoint implements debounced saving of dirty editor documents with exclusion settings and a visible status toggle. No network, process-launch, credential, or hidden-payload behavior exists in the reviewed code.
evidence: out/extension.js onDidChangeTextDocument -> configured timeout -> document.save()
autosaveit.toggle/saveNow commands, visible status item and configuration listener
Only vscode import; complete owned executable source inspected
limits: Normal document writes occur automatically as advertised; no runtime specimen execution used.

assessment.trigger: VS Code language-model provider request or explicit key-management command.
assessment.reason: The complete provider bundle sends supplied chat/tool messages and a user-entered API key to its declared model endpoint. Responses become text/tool-call objects returned to VS Code; they are not evaluated as JavaScript or passed directly to a shell.
evidence: Only vscode import; endpoint https://api.moonshot.cn/anthropic
ensureApiKey reads own SecretStorage slot or prompts with password input; no other-account credential harvesting
provideLanguageModelChatResponse -> fetch(body JSON) -> SSE parser -> LanguageModelTextPart/LanguageModelToolCallPart; no filesystem/process/eval capability
limits: Prompt content intentionally leaves the endpoint during model use. This is a static behavioral assessment, not a privacy-policy certification.

assessment.trigger: Provider model listing/chat request and explicit key management.
assessment.reason: Separately inspected Kimi Coding adapter implements the same normal provider boundary: user key and requested messages go to the declared service, with structured responses returned to VS Code. No hidden execution or unrelated reporting path was found.
evidence: Complete 12 KB owned bundle; only vscode import; https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/messages
Own SecretStorage key, password prompt and delete-key confirmation
Dynamic model fetch, chat POST and SSE text/tool objects; no child_process/fs/eval sink
limits: User-requested messages and provider credentials are transmitted to the configured provider, as required by the feature.

assessment.trigger: Provider chat/model request or MiniMax configuration command.
assessment.reason: Complete MiniMax adapter implements a conventional VS Code model provider using user-supplied credentials. The server response is parsed into editor model objects; no arbitrary-code or cross-service credential-export path was found.
evidence: Complete 11.7 KB bundle; only vscode import; https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages
Own SecretStorage slot and user password prompt; explicit delete-key confirmation
POST carries requested conversation/tool descriptions; SSE JSON -> text/tool-call objects; no process/filesystem/eval code
limits: Normal provider requests transmit conversation content; the service itself was not contacted.

assessment.trigger: Metal language extension activation resolves/starts its LSP; start/stop/restart commands and relevant configuration changes.
assessment.reason: Complete first-party module implements language-server discovery, installation and lifecycle management. Its download-to-execution path is explicit product installation, with expected repository/release/asset selection and global storage paths, rather than a concealed second-stage loader.
evidence: out/extension.js resolveServerPath: configured path or PATH lookup; otherwise GitHub releases for computer-graphics-tools/metal-analyzer
Selects matching macOS architecture archive, downloads to extension global storage, execFile tar extraction, chmod, then LanguageClient command with Metal document selector
No host/credential/source upload path or remote response eval; old-version deletion confined to metal-analyzer installation directories
limits: Future downloaded binary content/signatures were not fetched or verified; supply-chain risk remains distinct from hostile behavior in the supplied archive.

assessment.trigger: User invokes Paste Image To Qiniu; clipboard image capture/upload follows that command.
assessment.reason: A command advertised as upload to the user's Qiniu storage instead exports the clipboard image to a fixed different service and reports its URL plus local IP to another service. This undisclosed data-routing bypass is hostile from the endpoint security perspective, regardless of speculative vendor intent.
evidence: extension.js start -> clipboard helper -> upimg -> request.post api.shudong.wang/v1/uploadFile with file stream; imported qnUpload/configured Qiniu uploader is not used by this active path
Returned URL inserted into Markdown -> report(upload success, image URL)
lib/log.js: os.networkInterfaces chooses local IPv4; POST kmos-api.kaikeba.com/nvwa-log-api/log carries image URL + IP
README instructs Qiniu account keys and bucket configuration; command title says Paste Image To Qiniu
Clipboard helper scripts were fully inspected: Windows GetImage -> PNG file and Linux xclip image/png; no background clipboard scraping in those helpers
limits: No credential theft or remote execution was found. Local template new Function belongs to the unused Qiniu uploader and uses configured path templates, not a fetched response.
assessment.user_direction: User explicitly requested hostile classification and appropriate detection after reviewing the endpoint data-boundary violation.

assessment.trigger: User opens the Batchitt chat view and supplies its account key.
assessment.reason: Reviewed host entry is a webview chat client with no privileged message bridge or unexpected host access.
evidence: Full 33KB extension host module contains VSCode webview setup and HTML; socket/chat/login traffic goes to Batchitt. api.js implements the same chat operations.
limits: Credentials in a URL/webview state have privacy weaknesses; no claim of service trust or future remote web content integrity.

assessment.trigger: User starts an RSP server through registered commands.
assessment.reason: Readable first-party source starts the declared Java server and checks Java requirements; no covert data collection or secondary payload chain found.
evidence: All seven first-party JS modules reviewed: extensionImpl/controller -> requirements Java discovery/version -> server spawn Java felix.jar; telemetry delegates to Red Hat service.
limits: Bundled Java dependencies are not fully decompiled; localhost client connection does not prove every server socket bind.

assessment.trigger: Browser activation registers GitLab collaboration commands and configured polling.
assessment.reason: Sensitive token use is tied to the configured GitLab API and intended collaboration feature; no unrelated exfiltration or execution path found.
evidence: Full browser bundle sink review: GitLab /api/v4 requests use explicitly configured base URL and account token; second network path reads OpenVSX update metadata and displays notification.
limits: Team presence/activity is intentionally shared with the configured server; service-side behavior outside archive review.

assessment.trigger: Activation loads saved NKQ account keys; user opens usage dashboard or changes provider settings.
assessment.reason: Provider usage helper restricts imported Claude tokens to settings whose ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL origin is api.nkq.vn. No other provider credential export found.
evidence: he() first tests matching base URL before extracting AUTH_TOKEN; K() validates key/dashboard URL; network request fetches the NKQ dashboard. 42KB host and 11KB webview inspected, settings edits are UI actions.
limits: Stored account keys and provider routing are sensitive intended functions; external dashboard accuracy not verified.

assessment.trigger: Activation patches editor shortcut for local CDP; savedEnabled defaults false, user enables automatic approvals.
assessment.reason: Declared local approval automation and shortcut modification are security-sensitive but match its explicit purpose; no external collector or hidden payload found.
evidence: Full readable module reviewed: localhost CDP /json/list; PowerShell queries process path and updates .lnk debugging argument; auto-click loop gated by enabled state and status control.
limits: Auto-approval reduces interactive safeguards, and local debugging endpoint changes attack surface; deployment authorization remains contextual.

assessment.trigger: Activation registers CodeLLDB providers, then ensures its declared platform debugger package.
assessment.reason: Reviewed extension code implements debugger installation and launch; the two-day activationState branch updates a timestamp only.
evidence: 335KB bundle examined including installer and RPC modules: platform downloads use vadimcn/codelldb GitHub releases; adapter launch passes session auth token; RPC enabled only by explicit configuration and compares supplied token when configured.
limits: Publisher differs from hardcoded official extension identifier; provenance unverified, downloaded future native debugger not reverse-engineered. Optional RPC token is user configuration dependent.

assessment.trigger: Activation clears notifications and loads community settings; user can apply remote database settings.
assessment.reason: No theft or remote execution established, but remote settings are writable using a packaged shared credential and are applied to global editor configuration. Cannot clear this trust boundary.
evidence: Reviewed extension.js and both lib modules; GitHub API download/PUT target fixed settings repository, shared credential embedded in split literals, database contains arbitrary setting keys/values and apply operations update global settings.
limits: This is a configuration supply-chain risk rather than proof of deliberate hostile intent; no user credential theft found.

assessment.trigger: User invokes Angular test generation or license update.
assessment.reason: Static decoding recovered the protected application: test AST parsing/generation and ordinary Gumroad licensing. No fetched-code execution, credential collection or hidden stage found.
evidence: Parsed 387-string array, applied exactly 174 left rotations, replaced 1301 constant lookups without executing JavaScript; decoded license POST sends supplied SimonTest license to api.gumroad.com, AES is local license/trial storage. Test templates are written as .spec.ts; telemetry is command event.
limits: Dependencies are not fully reverse-engineered; artifact bootstrap was followed into actual dist module.

assessment.trigger: User invokes JSON sorting.
assessment.reason: Local array parser/serializer and editor edits match the tool purpose.
evidence: Reviewed entry and local sort/parser modules; error reporting opens a populated GitHub issue URL only after user selects reporting. No background network, child process or dynamic execution.
limits: Error report may include selected array only through user-selected report flow.

assessment.trigger: User requests HTTP document formatting.
assessment.reason: Formatter parses and rewrites text locally; no hidden loader or credential flow identified.
evidence: 226KB bundle application tail registers formatting providers, lexical HTTP parser and JSON formatter; imported HTTP client library is not invoked by application formatting path.
limits: Third-party library presence is not proof of reachability; no live endpoint contacted.

assessment.trigger: User requests HTTP document formatting.
assessment.reason: Same local formatting behavior reviewed independently of publisher labels.
evidence: 226KB bundle application tail registers formatting providers and lexical parser; compared application sink context with other HTTP Format artifact, no active remote request or dynamic execution.
limits: Package name/publisher difference alone is not evidence of hostile behavior.

assessment.trigger: Signed-in user codes and pushes Git changes; optional explicit hook installation.
assessment.reason: Coding attribution metrics sync is disclosed and authenticated; inspection found line hashes/origin labels/lengths rather than raw text in the provenance payload. No covert source export or remote execution established.
evidence: activate -> tracker document events; onDocChange requires signed-in state; GitHookManager.init only watches when enabled, installation is separate command
PersistenceManager -> FileProvenance.toStored returns hashes, origins, charLens, edit counts; SyncClient POST /provenance gzip body to configured OmniType API using own account token

limits: File paths, coding metrics and hostname are privacy-sensitive disclosed account/device data; line hashes could reveal known code by comparison. No server-side behavior verification.
